objective: Test whether small/mid-size Dynamics partners form a reachable channel for white-label EWS dependency triage before Exchange Online retirement.

official_deadline.note: Microsoft documents the end of Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement on-premises server-side synchronization with Exchange Online and recommends migration or temporary EWS allow-list continuity.

targets.name: Netzer Consulting
targets.evidence: Microsoft Dynamics partner; explicitly offers upgrades for Dynamics CRM/NAV/Axapta

targets.name: Izertis
targets.evidence: Historical Microsoft award as Spain's most ready CRM 2016 partner

targets.name: Dynamics 360
targets.evidence: Current support for CRM 2011-2016 on-premises plus migration and integration services

targets.name: Code8 Software
targets.evidence: Microsoft partner; explicitly advertises on-premise-to-cloud Dynamics migrations

targets.name: Hyper Talent Solutions
targets.evidence: Explicit Dynamics CRM v4/2011/2013/2015/2016 on-premise support and integration services

targets.name: Stallions Solutions
targets.evidence: Microsoft Dynamics CRM consultancy, support and cloud-migration services

targets.name: TechLabs London
targets.evidence: Dynamics CRM on-premise migration-to-cloud consultancy; public day rates

targets.name: Savaco
targets.evidence: Dedicated Dynamics CRM On-Premise to cloud service; experience since CRM 3.0
targets.note: Has in-house migration tooling; less likely white-label buyer.

targets.name: ARP Ideas
targets.evidence: Dedicated Dynamics CRM on-premise cloud migration offer

targets.name: arades
targets.evidence: Current page explicitly supports Dynamics CRM on-premise/hybrid deployment

targets.name: b4dynamics
targets.evidence: Microsoft Dynamics consultancy with on-premise and cloud customer base

targets.name: 3P Solutions

targets.name: Synchronicity Systems

targets.name: KPMG
targets.evidence: Explicit Dynamics CRM on-premise/private-cloud migration service
targets.note: Too large and self-sufficient for initial channel wedge.

interpretation: The channel hypothesis survives desk research. There are more than eight plausible partners and more than three with explicit legacy Dynamics CRM/on-premises work. However, this is distribution evidence, not willingness-to-pay. Do not build a public site yet. The next scarce evidence is whether partners will pay for or resell a standardized triage artifact rather than perform it themselves.

offer_refinement.name: Dynamics EWS Cutoff Triage Pack
offer_refinement.buyer: small/mid-size Dynamics partner or MSP with legacy CRM customers
offer_refinement.non_goal: Do not compete with full cloud migrations or generic Graph sync products.

next_gate.test: Obtain real market response from a small set of partners or identify public requests for this exact cutoff problem.
next_gate.pass: At least 2 partners show interest in a reusable assessment/white-label deliverable, or 1 asks for pricing/pilot.
next_gate.fail: Partners universally treat the assessment as trivial/in-house work or only want full cloud migration projects.
